note: Attacker-controlled ODP action text enters the parser as the raw input string.
The parser recognizes a push_nsh action and begins filling an NSH key structure from the input.
The default metadata type is initialized before optional fields are parsed.
For MD type 2, the parser copies attacker-supplied hex metadata into a local buffer and computes md_size from it.
The parsed NSH fields and metadata are serialized into a nested netlink action attribute.

code: if (nsh->mdtype == NSH_M_TYPE2) { if (metadata && md_size > 0) nl_msg_put_unspec(buf, OVS_NSH_KEY_ATTR_MD2, metadata, md_size); }
note: The serializer forwards the attacker-controlled metadata pointer and length into nl_msg_put_unspec for the MD2 attribute.

code: ptr = nl_msg_put_unspec_uninit(msg, type, size); nullable_memcpy(ptr, data, size);
note: The helper copies the attribute payload with nullable_memcpy, which is the sink named in the crash report.
The copy dereferences the supplied source buffer when size is non-zero, completing the vulnerable read path.
